Engineering Breakdown: How 2026 Toyota Sequoia (Limited / Platinum 4WD) Towing & Payload Math Works

When evaluating the 2026 Toyota Sequoia (Limited / Platinum 4WD) with the 3.4L i-FORCE MAX Hybrid V6 / 5.7L V8 (437 HP / 583 lb-ft torque, 3.31 axle ratio), buyers frequently look only at the advertised 9,120 lb maximum towing capacity. However, under SAE J2807 testing standards, factory tow ratings assume a base-trim vehicle with only a 150-lb driver and zero additional cargo or options.

1. The Payload Capacity Formula (GVWR minus Curb Weight)

Your legal vertical load ceiling is governed by the Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) of 7,570 lbs minus the Curb Weight of 6,150 lbs, yielding a maximum payload of 1,420 lbs. Every pound of trailer tongue weight (typically 12% to 15% of total trailer weight for bumper-pull campers, or 18% to 20% pin weight for fifth-wheels) presses directly down on the rear axle and subtracts from your available payload:

Available Payload for Tongue Weight = 1,420 lbs (Max Payload) - [Passengers + Truck Bed Cargo + Hitch Weight]
Payload-Limited Max Trailer Weight  = Available Payload for Tongue Weight ÷ 0.13 (Standard 13% Travel Trailer Tongue Ratio)

2. Why Payload Runs Out Before Max Tow Rating

If you load 550 lbs of family members, firewood, coolers, and a weight-distribution hitch into the 2026 Toyota Sequoia, you have 870 lbs of remaining payload capacity. Dividing that remaining payload by a 13% tongue weight ratio limits your maximum loaded travel trailer weight to 6,692 lbs—which is 2,428 lbs lower than the brochure tow number.
